desc:
Encoding. A singly linked list with n nodes is given by two arrays. The nodes are numbered 0..n-1; node 0 is the head, vals[i] is the value stored in node i and succ[i] is the number of the node after node i, or -1 if there is none. The node numbers say nothing about the order in the list: follow succ to find it.

Every node can be reached from the head. Following succ from node 0 either ends at -1 or, if the list has a cycle, the last node of the walk (the last node visited before a node would be visited again) points back to an earlier node of the walk.

Repair the list: if it has a cycle, replace the pointer of that last node by -1, so that the list ends there. Then return the values of the list from head to tail. A list without a cycle is returned unchanged.

Example: vals = [7,8,9,4], succ = [1,2,3,1] is 7 -> 8 -> 9 -> 4 -> 8 -> .... Node 3 (value 4) points back to node 1, so we cut that link and the answer is [7,8,9,4]. The point is to find that node without a visited set.
constraints: Every node is reachable from node 0
hints: Walking from the head with a visited set until you see a repeat shows the last node directly. Try to do it with O(1) extra memory.

First find the node where the cycle starts: a slow and a fast pointer meet inside the cycle, and a pointer restarted from the head together with the one at the meeting spot meet again at the entry node.

Once you know the entry node, walk around the cycle from it until you reach the node whose succ is the entry. That is the node to cut. Careful with a cycle of length 1 (a self loop) and with an entry node that is the head.
editorial: Phase 1: Floyd's tortoise and hare. If the fast pointer reaches -1 there is no cycle and the list is already fine. Otherwise the pointers meet inside the cycle.

Phase 2: put one pointer back on the head and leave the other at the meeting node; advancing both by one node per turn makes them meet exactly at the entry node of the cycle (the tail before the cycle has length a, and the meeting node is a multiple of the cycle length minus a steps before the entry, so the walks align after a steps).

Phase 3: from the entry node walk along the cycle until the next node is the entry again. This last node is the end of the list; set its successor to -1. Finally read out the values. Everything is O(n) time and O(1) extra space apart from the output.
solution:
def cutCycle(vals, succ):
    succ = succ[:]
    slow = fast = 0
    meet = -1
    while fast != -1 and succ[fast] != -1:
        slow = succ[slow]
        fast = succ[succ[fast]]
        if slow == fast:
            meet = slow
            break
    if meet != -1:
        entry, p = 0, meet
        while entry != p:
            entry = succ[entry]
            p = succ[p]
        last = entry
        while succ[last] != entry:
            last = succ[last]
        succ[last] = -1
    out = []
    cur = 0
    while cur != -1:
        out.append(vals[cur])
        cur = succ[cur]
    return out
